title: Scalp strands are dead keratinized cells, and melanin colors them
summary: OpenStax says the strands on the scalp are dead keratinized cells and get their color from melanin.
body: OpenStax lists those strands among accessory structures of the body. They are made of dead keratinized cells. Melanin pigments give them color. The chapter review does not give a count of strands or a rule for cutting them. This card is what the strands are made of and why they have color. It is not a claim about baldness.

sources.title: 5.2 Accessory Structures of the Skin, chapter review
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology, first edition, web view, CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase: hair is dead keratinized cells and gets its color from melanin.
